rundown: Blue Hens beat Phoenix 93-47 at Bob Carpenter Center in Newark, DE. Blue Hens led 49-21 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 100%).
Leading the way — Phoenix: Hasan Laws 7 pts; Tobias Reese 4 ast; Daniel Daughtry 7 reb. Blue Hens: Steven Solano 15 pts; Nick Petronio 5 ast; Kachi Nzeh 11 reb.
Where Blue Hens won it: they shot 56% to 25%, shot 29% from three to 15% and won the boards 56-28.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 17, 10:58 AM ET. It had Phoenix 54% and Blue Hens 46%, projecting Phoenix 73.6 – Blue Hens 72.4 (146 total, Phoenix by 1.2).

Final: Phoenix 47 – Blue Hens 93. Wrong winner: it had Phoenix at 54%, and Blue Hens (46%) won.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: WLSN pts scored, WLSN pts allowed, WLSN lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Phoenix came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 73.6, they scored 47 (−26.6 points, 36% under); projected to allow 72.4, they allowed 93 (+20.6 points, 28% over).

Blue Hens came in with a 5% below average attack and a league-average defense (2-2, 73.5 scored and 61.5 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 177 and 178 games of evidence. Projected to score 72.4, they scored 93 (+20.6 points, 28% over); projected to allow 73.6, they allowed 47 (−26.6 points, 36% under).

The bigger miss was Phoenix's scoring (-26.6 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 140 against 146 projected (-6), about the 34th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Blue Hens by 46 against Phoenix by 1.2 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (WLSN pts scored, WLSN pts allowed, WLSN lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.941 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +48.3 points. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 639 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.981 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Blue Hens attack ×0.982, defense ×0.960 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 47.2 points), no bet.
